prompt: What was state of the schools regarding integration in the hometown of Miller Williams when he began his master's degree in Zoology?
answer: When Miller Williams began his master’s degree in zoology at the University of Arkansas—around 1951–52—schools in his hometown of Hoxie were still racially segregated. Hoxie did not begin desegregating its public schools until July 1955, after *Brown v. Board of Education* (1954). It became one of Arkansas’s earliest—and most controversial—school-integration cases, provoking protests and a boycott by white residents.
